context: Answered Oct 28 02:36 CDT: no change. Keep today's flow: when the Mac and iPhone share wifi, install straight to the iPhone; otherwise TestFlight is the backup. Nothing is built (c91).

options.gain: Works from cloud merges with no Mac; the phone updates itself.
options.how: CI uploads each app to TestFlight when its main moves; the phone's TestFlight app updates it.
options.label: TestFlight on every merge
options.lose: TestFlight review and upload time, about 15 to 30 minutes; the Mac-first ruling becomes TestFlight-first.

options.how: A small Mac job notices main moved and installs the app when the phone is on the Mac's network.
options.label: A Mac watcher installs within minutes
options.lose: A background job on the Mac; nothing installs while the phone is away.

options.gain: Nothing runs behind your back; one step brings everything current.
options.how: You run one command (or tap one button) that installs every app whose main moved since the last install.
options.label: One command, any time
options.lose: You have to remember to run it.

options.gain: No churn on apps you are not using now.
options.how: Each app has an install switch; only switched-on apps install, by (b)'s watcher.
options.label: Only apps you are testing

title: How should a merged iOS change reach your phone?
why: It keeps the Mac-first ruling with nothing running unasked, which is what the earlier options got wrong; (a) is the fallback if you want no step at all.
